title: Alive, but not working
lede: A heartbeat proves the client is alive, not that it works.
why: Preemption is cooperative. iris does not kill running GPU work: it asks first, waits, and only then withdraws the reservation. Reclaiming is off by default; this recording turns it on.

d.reason: waiting for 16000 MB on rtx3090: nothing idle to evict
reclaimed: no GPU activity for 47 min
evicting comfyui on rtx3090 for 7836 MB

logs.reason: reclaimed: no GPU activity for 47 min

logs.detail: 410 MB still held (CUDA context or allocator cache): a restart frees it

beats.title: A big job on ComfyUI
beats.text: An evaluation run reserves 16.6 GB and starts rendering.

beats.title: The work stops. The heartbeats do not.
beats.text: The job died, but the loop that sends its heartbeats lives on. To a simple broker this lease looks perfectly healthy. iris also watches the GPU, and ComfyUI's queue is empty.

beats.title: Flagged as stalled
beats.text: After 30 minutes with no sign of GPU work, the lease is marked stalled. Nothing is taken away yet: nobody else wants the card.

beats.title: Now it is in the way, so it is asked to leave
beats.text: argus-atlas queues behind the stalled lease. Every heartbeat reply now carries yield_requested. A live client would let go at its next safe point. iris does not kill running GPU work.

beats.title: Asked for 15 minutes, then reclaimed
beats.text: The request was ignored, so the reservation ends: “reclaimed: no GPU activity for 47 min”. Resuming that lease is refused too, so a zombie loop cannot take it back.

beats.title: And the card goes back to work
beats.text: iris unloads the model ComfyUI had cached, waits for the GPU to confirm, and grants the bake. In the real incident behind this scene, a dead job's 17 GB lease kept beating for 1 h 38 min and blocked a map bake. That is why the watchdog exists.
